title: Final Fantasy VII Began as a Detective Story in New York
hook:
The first draft of Final Fantasy VII had no Midgar and no Buster Sword. It starred a detective named Joe chasing reactor bombers through New York City, and one of those bombers slowly turned into Cloud. Would you have played that version?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloud_Strife (citing Polygon, Final Fantasy 7: An oral history, 2017)
script: Did you know Final Fantasy Seven, the nineteen ninety seven classic, started out as a detective story set in New York City? Before Midgar existed, series creator Hironobu Sakaguchi wrote the very first plot treatment himself. It was not set on a fantasy world at all. It took place in modern day New York. The hero was a detective named Joe. He was investigating a group that wanted to destroy the city's Mako reactors. One member of that group was an early sketch of the character who eventually became Cloud Strife. Tetsuya Nomura, who designed the cast, has described that first draft in interviews. As the story grew, the detective angle was dropped. The reactors stayed, but the team moved them into a fictional city called Midgar. In the finished game you play as the group bombing the reactors, not the man chasing them. The New York idea did not vanish completely either. Sakaguchi has said it may have fed into Parasite Eve. That Square game is set in New York and came out a year after Final Fantasy Seven. So one of the most famous role playing games ever made almost opened with a detective's badge instead of a giant sword. Which version would you rather have played? Follow for more gaming history.
